meta.title: The Economics of Cognitive Extraction
meta.description: Moving beyond the 'distraction' trope, we explore how platforms utilize predictive arbitrage to commodify the gap between your intention and your action.

scenes.title: The Intentionality Gap
scenes.say: Why does focus feel impossible? It is not a failure of your character or willpower; it is a systematic extraction of your cognitive energy by design.

scenes.text:
Your focus is an
arbitrage opportunity.
scenes.say: Platforms operate on the 'intentionality gap'—the profit margin between what you intended to do and the algorithmic detour they successfully sell to advertisers.
Algorithms are calibrated to intercept your executive function within a 4-second window, exploiting biological reaction times before you can consciously reassert control.

scenes.title: Predictive Arbitrage
scenes.say: This isn't just about dopamine hits; it is high-frequency trading where your attention is the asset class and your behavior is the commodity.
Platforms treat your future actions as tradable futures. They don't just predict what you want; they engineer the environment to ensure your behavior meets their growth projections.
With predictive accuracy exceeding 85%, the platform effectively removes your autonomy, turning your 'choices' into predictable inputs for their revenue models.

scenes.title: Economic Resistance
scenes.say: Reclaiming your focus is not a self-help project; it is an act of economic defiance against an infrastructure built to harvest your mental labor.

scenes.text:
1. Increase friction
2. De-couple identity
3. Value non-data
scenes.say: We must introduce 'economic friction' by starving the algorithm of data, opting for offline systems, and refusing to participate in the metrics that turn our lives into inventory.
When you choose focus, you are choosing to withhold your cognitive capital from an extraction machine. It is the ultimate market rebellion.
Stop financing their business model with your attention. Reclaim your cognitive capital.
